extracted.intended_audience: Magma users (beginners to intermediate) seeking guidance on the online help browser, string handling, printing, and related intrinsics
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and usage rules for Magma's online help browser, string data type and operations, printing (print/printf/Sprint), regular expressions, and verbosity controls. Includes command behaviors, escape sequences, conversion functions, and recommended practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Help Nodes (O, S, I, E)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four kinds of help nodes: Overview (O), Section (S), Intrinsic (I) and Example (E). O nodes are purpose-written for the online help and, if an O node exists for a topic, it should be read before other nodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The help system states the kind of each node when showing contents or listing search results. S, I and E correspond to Handbook sources; O nodes are terser and aimed at relative beginners. Read O nodes first when present to get the intended quick overview before diving into S/I/E nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricting find/delve/walk/back by node kind
rubrics_metrics.description: The find, delve, walk and back commands may be restricted to select only one kind of node using prefixed variants (ofind, sfind, ifind, efind, odelve, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use e.g. ifind to find only Intrinsic (I) nodes when looking for intrinsic functions like Field; this narrows results to the desired node kinds and reduces noise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references via +n
rubrics_metrics.description: Some nodes give cross-references with special numbers beginning with a + symbol; these indicate related or directly-subordinate nodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references are usually listed at the end of a node's contents; type '+<number>' at the browser prompt to read the referenced node (e.g., +1). A few cross-references may also appear in the node body and can be followed the same way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tab-completion behavior in the browser
rubrics_metrics.description: Pressing Tab causes the browser to consider the word at or just after the cursor and attempt completions; behavior depends on whether there are zero, one, or multiple possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no possibilities: a beep. If one possibility: the word is completed. If several: a beep and expansion to the common prefix; pressing Tab again lists all possible completions and repeats the input line so the user can finish it. Tab completion is available in many contexts for fast navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tab-completion typing strategy (minimal typing)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using tab completion, type as little as possible of the beginning of the word so as not to miss anything relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typing too much can exclude relevant items that do not share the same initial letters (case-insensitive). There is a trade-off: shorter prefixes yield more (possibly irrelevant) matches; longer prefixes reduce noise but risk missing relevant references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline pathname browsing with repeated tabs
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of tab completions on a pathname can be used for quick inline browsing with few keystrokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show gradually building a path by typing '/' then partial segments and repeatedly using Tab to expand to candidates and eventually reach the desired node (e.g., show /magma/group/matrix/Boolean/...). This speeds navigation through the help-tree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprinting recent find/delve/search results (numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The numbers command reprints the list of nodes from the most recent find, delve or search command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when you've viewed some nodes from a list and forgotten the numbers of other nodes; use numbers to recall the current numbering range and then show a desired item by number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking and recalling nodes (mark/unmark/marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can mark nodes for later reading using mark (which assigns them node specifications like '1, and later recall them via the 'n notation); marks persist for the Magma session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mark <number> to create a permanent-in-session reference 'i for that node; use 'i to show it later. unmark removes a mark; marks lists the current marks. This is helpful to track useful nodes across other work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Browser command abbreviation and ambiguity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Every browser command may be abbreviated to a substring with which it begins; if multiple commands share that substring, the browser chooses the alphabetically first command (exceptions: 's' for show and 'e' for exit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that short abbreviations may map to unintended commands if ambiguous; use a longer unique prefix when needed. Examples: d (delve), f (find), iw (walk along intrinsics), sb (back along sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Node specification forms for commands
rubrics_metrics.description: A node specification n (used in many commands) can be an absolute pathname, a pathname relative to the current node, an integer in the current numbers range, a cross-reference (+n), a mark ('n), or the '"' character indicating the last-node referred to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate form when invoking show, walk, goto, etc.; relative pathnames (e.g., iteration/while) are convenient when inside a subtree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-help requests using ?
rubrics_metrics.description: A single help request starting with ? acts like a find or show: if followed by a reference word it performs a find (and if exactly one match, also a show); if followed by a pathname, number, or cross-reference it performs a show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ?/system/time shows the /system/time node. Single-help requests may be made inside the browser, but they operate somewhat independently (they do not change the " last-node character).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tab completion after ? available only outside browser
rubrics_metrics.description: Tab completion following the ? single-help-request is available only outside the browser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ? with tab completion from the Magma level (outside browser) to benefit from pathname/word completions when issuing single help requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: String literal syntax (double quotes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Literal strings must be enclosed in double quotation marks (" "). Every character in a string is significant, including spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print "The result..."; string equality is sensitive to exact characters (including spaces). Assign strings to identifiers as usual: ResultStr := "...".

rubrics_metrics.name: String immutability and use of sequences for modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike sequences, strings cannot be mutated by assignment to an index (you cannot assign to s[i]); to perform complex modifications (change parts, reorder, count characters) convert the string to a sequence of characters, manipulate that sequence, and convert back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use helper functions StringToSequence and SequenceToString (or &* reduction) for conversions. This is the recommended approach for sophisticated string operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic string operations and their meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental string operators/functions include: #s (length), s[i] (ith character), Substring(s,n,k), s * t or s cat t (concatenation), s^n (repeat), Position(s,t)/Index(s,t) (first position of t in s), relational operators eq/ne/in/notin/lt/le/gt/ge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 12.1 enumerates these operations and expected semantics. Use cat or * for concatenation; Position returns 0 when substring absent (special case: Position(s,"") returns 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Escape sequences and special characters in strings
rubrics_metrics.description: Special characters are inserted via backslash escapes: \t (tab), \n or \r (newline/return), \" (double-quote), \\ (backslash), and backslash+<return> for line continuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To include a double quotation mark inside a string use \"; to include a backslash use \\; use the listed escapes to format output (tabs/newlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line continuation with backslash and return
rubrics_metrics.description: If a backslash is followed immediately by the return key, Magma ignores both the backslash and the return internally (line continuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for breaking long input lines (string literals or other input) across multiple typed lines while Magma treats them as a single logical line. Works both inside and outside strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: String↔sequence conversions and character codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use StringToSequence to turn a string into a sequence of one-character strings, and SequenceToString (or &* reduction) to rebuild a string. Use StringToCode and CodeToString to convert between one-character strings and their character codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conversions enable transformations such as case conversion (example LowerToUpperCase) and other character-level processing. Error checks (e.g., verifying characters are in 'a'..'z') should be used to avoid runtime errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Split(s,d) semantics and special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Split(s,d) splits string s into a sequence of substrings separated by runs of characters from delimiter string d; delimiter characters are not included in the results. If s is empty, Split(s,d) returns an empty sequence. Split(s) (no delimiter) splits on newline characters (distinct lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delimiter d is treated as a set of characters (e.g., " \t\n" for whitespace). Example: Split("qj23jk...","1234567890") yields letter-only substrings. Use Split(s) to get lines of a multi-line string.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regexp(r,s) return values and grouping behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Regexp(r, s) tests whether s matches the regular expression r. If true it returns additionally the matched substring and a sequence of substrings corresponding to parenthesized groups in r. Parentheses restrict scope and cause captured-group substrings to be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regexp uses a V8-style regex implementation; table of special regex symbols is provided (., *, +, ?, ^, $, character classes, escapes, grouping). Example: Regexp(" (.*) ([0-9][0-9]?) .*EST (....)", date) extracts month, day, year from a date string.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print statement levels (Minimal, Default, Maximal, Magma)
rubrics_metrics.description: print expression,...(: level) supports four levels: Minimal, Default, Maximal, and Magma. The level controls the quantity/detail of output; omitting the level defaults to Default. Magma level produces Magma-readable output (can be copy-pasted back into Magma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Minimal for compact descriptions, Maximal for verbose human-readable details, and Magma when you need a representation that can be parsed back by Magma. Examples given for MatrixAlgebra, groups, and designs illustrate differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sprint(x, L) returns printed output as a string for a given level
rubrics_metrics.description: Sprint(x) returns the string that would be printed by print x (Default). Sprint(x, L) returns the string for the specified printing level L ("Minimal","Default","Maximal","Magma").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Sprint to capture object descriptions for parsing or further processing, e.g., use Regexp on Sprint output to extract numeric or structural information from printed representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbose printing flags and control functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many major algorithms offer verbose printing controlled by named flags. By default verbosity flags are off. SetVerbose(name, x) changes a flag; GetVerbose(name) returns its current setting. There are five spare flags 'User1'..'User5'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flags with only two settings: use 0/false for off, 1/true for on. Flags with multiple levels: 0/false means off, small positive integers denote increasing verbosity levels, and true denotes the minimum non-zero verbosity. Use these to request progress information during long computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printf format rules and placeholders (%o and %m)
rubrics_metrics.description: printf takes a format string and expressions. The format string must contain %o (object: Default printing) and/or %m (Magma printing) placeholders the same number of times as there are expressions. Newlines are not implicit; include \n explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: %o prints expressions in Default mode, %m prints in Magma mode. Because printf does not automatically add a newline, include '\n' when needed; Magma will flush and print a newline automatically if a prompt is due and output is buffered, but explicit newlines are good practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print flushing behavior when prompt imminent
rubrics_metrics.description: If Magma is about to give a prompt and there is output waiting in the printf buffer, Magma flushes the buffer (prints the text) and performs a newline before giving the prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While this auto-flush can add a newline even if you omitted \n, rely on explicit '\n' for predictable output formatting across contexts.
